2609.20659.title: HIL-UMI: Bringing Human-in-the-Loop Post-Training of Vision-Language-Action Models to Universal Manipulation Interface
2609.20659.paper_summary: Large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models provide powerful priors for robot manipulation, yet adapting them to a specific deployment remains challenging. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on task-specific demonstrations provides a step toward deployment, but faces two persistent limitations: static data provide limited coverage of out-of-distribution states, and standard imitation objectives do not distinguish progressing behavior from less useful data. Interactive post-training can address these limitations, but typically requires repeated policy execution and human intervention on a physical robot. We introduce HIL-UMI, a policy-guided Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) framework for robot-free human-in-the-loop VLA post-training. During handheld UMI demonstrations, HIL-UMI queries the current policy on the same observation stream without executing its predictions. The Energy Score compares the human action trajectory with policy inference and triggers collection when their discrepancy indicates an out-of-distribution region. In a separate feedback loop, low online advantage predictions identify essential segments for refining a progress-based advantage estimator. The updated estimator then guides advantage-conditioned behavioral cloning using a balanced mixture of base demonstrations and new policy data. This design preserves the iterative and policy-aware nature of human-in-the-loop learning while decoupling data collection from robot deployment. Experiments on four real-world tasks spanning long-horizon and precise manipulation show that HIL-UMI achieves consistent improvement over SFT and benefits from both targeted collection and advantage refinement. Moreover, HIL-UMI outperforms HG-DAgger on Clean Up Table with lower per-frame collection time, suggesting a scalable path for VLA post-training across operators and locations.
2609.20659.paper_summary_zh: 大型視覺-語言-行動（VLA）模型為機器人操作提供了強大的先驗，但將其適應於特定部署仍然具有挑戰性。針對任務特定示範的監督微調（SFT）為部署提供了一個步驟，但面臨兩個持續的限制：靜態數據對分佈外狀態的覆蓋有限，且標準模仿目標無法區分進展行為與較不有用數據。互動後訓練可以解決這些限制，但通常需要在實體機器人上重複執行策略和人類干預。我們介紹了HIL-UMI，一個政策引導的通用操作介面（UMI）框架，用於無機器人的人類參與VLA後訓練。在手持UMI示範期間，HIL-UMI在相同的觀察流上查詢當前政策，而不執行其預測。能量分數比較人類行動軌跡與政策推斷，並在它們的差異顯示出分佈外區域時觸發收集。在一個單獨的反饋迴路中，低在線優勢預測識別出精煉基於進展的優勢估計器所需的關鍵片段。然後，更新的估計器引導基於優勢條件的行為克隆，使用基礎示範和新政策數據的平衡混合。這一設計保留了人類參與學習的迭代和政策感知特性，同時將數據收集與機器人部署解耦。對於四個涵蓋長期和精確操作的現實世界任務的實驗顯示，HIL-UMI在SFT上實現了一致的改進，並受益於針對性的收集和優勢精煉。此外，HIL-UMI在清理桌子任務上以較低的每幀收集時間超越了HG-DAgger，這表明了VLA後訓練在操作員和地點之間擴展的可行途徑。
